groups.sentence: Instructors provide an alternative assignment or non-AI pathway with the same learning goals for students who cannot or do not want to use AI.
Instructors consider equity, access, cost and accessibility when designing policies or choosing AI tools.
Instructors ensure all students have equitable access to the AI tools used in their course.
Instructors provide no-cost or institutionally supported AI tools and verify free versions are sufficient.
Instructors do not prohibit or replace approved accommodations and assistive technologies.
Faculty and the university ensure AI use has no disparate impact on students with disabilities.
Instructors do not require students to purchase a paid AI subscription.
Instructors do not require students to create accounts with external or non-university AI tools.
Instructors do not mandate that students use AI tools.
Students talk to their instructor about access concerns, accommodations or alternatives.
Instructors tell students in the syllabus or course description what required AI tools will cost.
Instructors clarify how accommodations fit course AI expectations and involve accessibility offices.
Everyone can opt out of AI use without negative consequences.
Students may choose not to use AI if it is a barrier or they prefer not to.
Students use only AI tools that are free or provided to them.
Students are expected to obtain an AI account or pay for the most advanced version.
Instructors keep revisiting how they ask students to use AI with respect to access.
Paid AI tools and unequal access create inequity among students.
The university ensures equitable access to AI tools and resources for everyone.
Administrators state a commitment to accessible, equitable and inclusive AI.
The university provides students free access to some AI tools and support spaces.
AI use is optional, and students are not required to use or pay for tools.
The university provides no-cost or affordable AI tools and computing resources to students.
Approved disability accommodations and assistive technologies are not restricted by AI rules.
Alternatives are usually provided to students with concerns about access or privacy.
